items.title: Road Salt
items.text: Every winter, city workers spread salt on roads and sidewalks. The reason is simple: salt lowers the temperature at which water freezes, so ice melts even when the air is below zero. As a result, accidents drop and buses keep running. However, this solution has a hidden cost. When the snow melts, the salty water flows into the soil and nearby streams. Young trees along busy roads often turn brown in spring because their roots cannot take in enough water from salty ground. Salt also speeds up rust on cars and bridges, which means higher repair bills. Some towns therefore mix the salt with sand or sprinkle it only on the most dangerous hills and corners. Others use a liquid made from sugar beets, which harms nature less, although it is more expensive to buy. Safety clearly matters most, but careful use lets towns protect people without damaging the places they live in.

qs.q: According to the passage, why do young trees beside busy roads often turn brown?
o: Passing cars spray hot water onto them every morning.
Their roots cannot absorb enough water from salty soil.
Workers cut their branches before the spring comes.
Sand mixed with the salt covers all of their leaves.
qs.why: 본문에 '뿌리가 짠 땅에서 물을 충분히 빨아들이지 못해서' 갈색이 된다고 나와요. 원인과 결과를 연결하는 문제예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the liquid made from sugar beets?
o: It melts ice faster than salt does in every kind of weather.
It is cheaper than salt, but it is harder to spread on roads.
Towns must weigh its smaller harm to nature against its higher price.
It protects bridges from rust, but it kills the nearby trees.
qs.why: 'harms nature less, although it is more expensive'에서 자연에 덜 해롭지만 값이 더 비싸다는 것을 알 수 있어요. 나머지는 본문에 근거가 없어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the phrase 'a hidden cost' means a harm that is...
o: written on a price label.
paid before the work begins.
not obvious at first.
shared equally by all workers.
qs.why: 'hidden'은 '숨겨진'이라는 뜻이고, 바로 뒤에 처음에는 보이지 않는 피해(나무, 녹)가 설명돼요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'Others use a liquid made from sugar beets, which harms nature less', what does 'which' refer to?
o: the salt that workers spread
a liquid made from sugar beets
the sand mixed with the salt
the water that flows into streams
qs.why: 관계대명사 which는 바로 앞의 'a liquid made from sugar beets'를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Road salt keeps people safe, but towns need to limit its side effects.
Salt should be banned because it destroys every young tree in town.
Sugar beets are the best answer to all of the winter problems.
Accidents fall only when towns use sand instead of any salt.
qs.why: 소금이 안전에 도움이 되지만 부작용이 있어 조심해서 써야 한다는 것이 글 전체의 요지예요.

items.title: Lights and Turtles
items.text: On many beaches, baby sea turtles hatch at night. Instinct tells them to crawl toward the brightest part of the horizon, which in nature is the moonlit sea. Today, though, hotels and streetlights often shine brighter than the moon, so hatchlings sometimes turn the wrong way and crawl toward roads instead. Many are lost before sunrise. To solve the problem, some coastal towns have changed their lamps. Amber lights, for instance, confuse turtles far less than white ones, and shields on the lamps keep the glow from spreading toward the sand. Volunteers also walk the beach during the hatching season, gently guiding lost babies to the water. Not everyone welcomes these changes. Some hotel owners worry that darker beaches will feel less safe to their guests. Even so, the number of hatchlings reaching the sea has risen in places that adopted the new lamps, which suggests that small adjustments can make a large difference.

qs.q: According to the passage, why do some hatchlings crawl toward roads?
o: Artificial lights look brighter to them than the moonlit sea.
The sand near the roads stays warmer than the sea through the night.
Volunteers carry them away from the water by mistake at night.
They follow the noise of cars passing along the beach road.
qs.why: 본능적으로 가장 밝은 쪽으로 가는데, 호텔과 가로등이 달보다 더 밝아서 길 쪽으로 간다고 설명돼요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about beaches with no bright artificial lights?
o: Volunteers there would no longer be allowed to help the babies.
The moon there would never shine on the water at night.
Hotels there would lose most of their guests every summer.
Hatchlings there are more likely to find the sea on their own.
qs.why: 달빛이 가장 밝은 곳이 되면 새끼 거북이 스스로 바다를 찾기 쉬울 것이라고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'shields' on the lamps are best described as...
o: signs that warn visitors to keep away from sea turtles.
walls that keep land animals off the sandy beach.
covers that stop light from going in certain directions.
bulbs that make the glow much stronger than before.
qs.why: shields가 '모래 쪽으로 빛이 퍼지는 것을 막는다'고 했으므로 빛을 가리는 덮개를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does 'these changes' in 'Not everyone welcomes these changes' refer to?
o: the new lamps and the way they are used near the beach
the instincts that baby turtles follow at night
the number of guests who are staying at hotels
the walks that hatchlings take across the sand
qs.why: 앞 문장들에서 설명한 램프 교체와 차폐 장치를 가리키며, 이어서 호텔 주인들의 걱정이 나와요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention the hotel owners' worry?
o: To show that the solution has some opponents.
To prove that the new lamps have failed completely.
To explain why turtles prefer the beaches near hotels.
To advise guests to avoid dark beaches in summer.
qs.why: 'Not everyone welcomes'로 시작해 반대 의견도 있음을 보여 주는 양보의 역할이고, 이어 'Even so'로 결과를 말해요.

items.title: No More Late Fees
items.text: For decades, libraries charged a small fine for every day a book was late. The idea seemed fair: if borrowers had to pay, they would return books on time. Yet several libraries that stopped charging fines have reported a surprising result. Overdue books came back at almost the same rate as before. What changed was who walked through the door. Families who once avoided the library because they owed money returned, and the number of active cardholders grew. In other words, the fines had not really made people responsible; they had mostly kept the poorest readers away. Of course, there are worries. Some librarians fear that books will stay out longer and that fewer copies will be available for others. Because of this, many libraries now send friendly reminders and set a limit on how many items a person can borrow at once. Their experience suggests that kindness can work as well as punishment, and sometimes better.

qs.q: What happened in libraries that stopped charging late fines?
o: Far fewer people borrowed books from the library shelves.
Books were returned at nearly the same rate as before.
Most borrowers kept their books for a whole year or more.
The libraries lost so much money that they closed early.
qs.why: 'Overdue books came back at almost the same rate as before'라고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the families who 'once avoided the library'?
o: They never enjoyed reading in any form, even at home.
They preferred to buy their books in large shops.
They moved to another town after they paid the fines.
They stayed away because they could not afford to pay fines.
qs.why: 연체료를 내야 해서 도서관을 피했던 가족들이 돌아왔고, 벌금이 가난한 독자를 쫓아냈다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'overdue' means...
o: too old and worn to be borrowed again by anyone.
not returned by the date it was expected.
missing from the shelf without any notice to staff.
damaged by water or by careless use at home.
qs.why: overdue는 '기한이 지난'이라는 뜻으로, 반납 기한을 넘긴 책을 말해요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'they had mostly kept the poorest readers away', what does 'they' refer to?
o: the libraries
the librarians
the cardholders
the fines
qs.why: 'the fines had not really made people responsible; they had mostly kept ... away'에서 they는 the fines예요.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose in the passage?
o: To warn readers that libraries will soon charge much higher fines.
To explain how librarians choose which books they should buy.
To show that dropping a punishment can work better than keeping it.
To argue that every borrower should be limited to one book.
qs.why: 벌금을 없앴더니 결과가 비슷하거나 오히려 좋았다는 것을 보여 주는 글이에요.

items.title: Paper Straws
items.text: When many restaurants replaced plastic straws with paper ones, customers had mixed feelings. On the one hand, plastic straws are used for only a few minutes but can last for hundreds of years in the environment, and they often end up in the sea. Paper straws break down much more quickly, so they seem like a clear improvement. On the other hand, some people complain that paper straws turn soft in a cold drink. A few restaurants have therefore tried straws made from rice or seaweed, which stay firm longer and can even be eaten. These cost more, however, and not every shop can afford them. Meanwhile, environmental groups point out that straws are a very small part of all plastic waste. For them, the most important step is to stop using things once and throwing them away, whether the material is plastic or paper. A reusable metal or glass straw, they say, solves the problem at its root.

qs.q: Why do some people complain about paper straws?
o: They are more expensive than rice straws.
They last for hundreds of years in the sea.
They can be eaten only after a few minutes.
They become soft in cold drinks.
qs.why: 'paper straws turn soft in a cold drink'라고 불평의 이유가 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the environmental groups' view?
o: Changing the material alone will not fix the larger waste problem.
Paper straws are worse for the natural world than plastic ones.
Restaurants should stop serving cold drinks to their guests.
Seaweed straws are the cheapest choice for small shops.
qs.why: 일회용품 자체를 줄이는 것이 중요하다고 했으므로, 재질만 바꾸는 것으로는 충분하지 않다는 추론이 가능해요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'at its root' means...
o: at the very bottom of the drink in the glass.
at the oldest and darkest part of the shop.
at the farthest end of the straw.
at the basic cause of the problem.
qs.why: solves the problem at its root는 '문제를 근본 원인에서 해결한다'는 뜻의 표현이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'These cost more, however', what does 'These' refer to?
o: straws made from rice or seaweed
paper straws from restaurants
reusable metal or glass straws
plastic straws used for a few minutes
qs.why: 앞 문장의 'straws made from rice or seaweed'를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Paper straws are the perfect answer to all of the ocean waste.
Customers should refuse every kind of straw in restaurants and cafés.
Rice and seaweed straws will soon replace every other material.
Swapping straws helps a little, but single-use habits matter more.
qs.why: 빨대 교체의 장단점을 비교하고 결국 일회용 습관이 근본 문제라는 결론으로 이어지는 글이에요.

items.title: Snacks in the Machine
items.text: Last year, our school changed the snacks in its vending machine. Chocolate bars and sugary drinks were replaced by fruit cups, nuts and sparkling water. The principal explained that students were skipping lunch and filling up on sweets instead, which left them tired in afternoon classes. At first, sales dropped sharply, and many students were annoyed. Some even walked to the shop across the street. Gradually, though, the situation changed. The new snacks were placed at eye level and priced lower than the old ones, so more students tried them. Teachers noticed that fewer people fell asleep after lunch. Still, the change is not perfect. A few students complain that fruit cups are too small to feel like a real snack, and the machine now makes less money for the student fund. The council is discussing a compromise: keeping one shelf for a small sweet treat, so that students feel they still have a choice.

qs.q: Why did the principal change the vending machine's snacks?
o: Students asked for fruit cups in a school survey.
The shop across the street had closed down.
The old machine had broken and could not be repaired.
Students were filling up on sweets and feeling tired in class.
qs.why: 교장 선생님은 학생들이 점심 대신 단것으로 배를 채워 오후 수업에 피곤해한다고 설명했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the compromise the council is discussing?
o: It will remove the fruit cups from the machine.
It aims to reduce complaints without the old problem.
It will raise the price of every snack.
It will let students leave school to buy lunch.
qs.why: 작은 단 간식 한 칸만 두는 절충안은 불만을 줄이면서도 이전 문제로 완전히 돌아가지 않으려는 것이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'a compromise' is...
o: a rule that nobody is allowed to change.
a solution in which each side accepts a little less.
a prize given to the winning group.
a mistake that is quickly corrected.
qs.why: compromise는 양쪽이 조금씩 양보하는 절충안을 뜻해요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'so more students tried them', what does 'them' refer to?
o: the sweets
the new snacks
the teachers
the afternoon classes
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장의 'The new snacks'를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the sentence 'Still, the change is not perfect'?
o: To explain why sales dropped at first.
To praise the principal's decision.
To describe how the machine works.
To introduce some problems that remain.
qs.why: 'Still'은 앞의 긍정적 결과에 대해 남은 문제점을 소개하는 역접 표현이에요.

items.title: Too Many Visitors
items.text: The small island of Lantern Bay once had fewer than two thousand residents and a handful of guesthouses. After photographs of its white cliffs spread online, visitors began arriving by the thousands each summer. At first, shop owners were delighted, because tourism brought jobs and income. Soon, however, problems appeared. Rents rose, so many young families could no longer afford to live there. The narrow paths were crowded, and the water supply sometimes ran short in August. Residents began to feel like strangers in their own village. In response, the local government introduced a daily limit on boat tickets and a small fee for day visitors. The money pays for path repairs and a new water tank. Not everyone is happy: some café owners say they lose customers on days when the tickets sell out. Even so, most residents agree that a quieter island is worth a smaller profit, because it keeps the place worth visiting.

qs.q: What caused the sudden rise in visitors to Lantern Bay?
o: The government built a large new harbor.
Photographs of its cliffs spread online.
A famous festival began to be held every August.
The guesthouses lowered their prices sharply.
qs.why: 'After photographs of its white cliffs spread online' 때문에 방문객이 늘었다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the café owners' complaint?
o: They want the island to have no visitors at all.
They believe the ticket fee is spent on their cafés.
They earn less when the number of visitors is capped.
They plan to move their businesses to a bigger island.
qs.why: 표가 매진되는 날 손님을 잃는다는 불만은 방문객 수 제한이 수입을 줄인다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'a handful of' guesthouses means...
o: a great many
an exact number of
a few
a growing list of
qs.why: a handful of는 '소수의, 몇 개의'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'The money pays for path repairs', what does 'The money' refer to?
o: the rent paid by young families
the income of the café owners
the fee paid by day visitors
the price of a guesthouse room
qs.why: 앞 문장의 'a small fee for day visitors'에서 걷힌 돈을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the main point of the last sentence?
o: A smaller profit is acceptable if it keeps the island pleasant.
The island should stop all tourism immediately and for good.
Day visitors are more welcome than overnight guests.
Café owners must accept lower prices for their coffee.
qs.why: 'a quieter island is worth a smaller profit'이 마지막 문장의 핵심이에요.

items.title: The Last Keepers
items.text: For centuries, lighthouse keepers lived on rocky coasts, climbing the stairs each evening to light the great lamp. The work was lonely and sometimes dangerous, but ships depended on it. In the twentieth century, automatic systems were developed, and the keepers were gradually no longer needed. A machine can switch on a lamp at sunset, measure fog and send a warning signal without anyone sleeping in the tower. Naturally, this saves money, and it is also safer for workers. Yet some people regret the change. A keeper could see a boat in trouble and call for help; a machine can only report what it has been built to measure. Others point out that old towers need constant care, and without residents they fall into ruin. Several have been turned into small museums or guesthouses, which pay for repairs. In this way, a job has disappeared, but a part of its history has been preserved.

qs.q: Why were lighthouse keepers gradually no longer needed?
o: Automatic systems could do the main tasks without people.
Ships stopped traveling along the rocky coasts for good.
The lamps were replaced by stars that are brighter.
Keepers refused to work in such lonely places any longer.
qs.why: 자동 시스템이 등불을 켜고 안개를 재고 경고 신호를 보낼 수 있게 되었기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about a machine compared with a keeper?
o: It is more dangerous for ships that pass by at night.
It cannot notice a problem it was not built to measure.
It costs more money to run than a human worker does.
It can call for help in every kind of emergency.
qs.why: 기계는 측정하도록 만들어진 것만 보고할 수 있다고 했으므로 예상 밖의 상황은 알아채지 못해요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'fall into ruin' means...
o: gradually become damaged and unusable.
become famous all around the world for its beauty.
be sold to a wealthy owner for a high price.
change into a modern building with new walls.
qs.why: fall into ruin은 관리되지 않아 점점 낡고 쓸 수 없게 되는 것을 말해요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'Several have been turned into small museums', what does 'Several' refer to?
o: several experienced lighthouse keepers
several old lighthouse towers
several automatic warning systems
several dangerous rocky coasts
qs.why: 앞 문장의 'old towers'를 받아 '여러 개의 오래된 등대 탑'을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose in the passage?
o: To describe how technology changed a job and what was kept from it.
To argue that lighthouses are no longer necessary anywhere.
To teach readers how to climb a tall tower safely.
To compare two coasts that have different kinds of weather.
qs.why: 기술 때문에 직업이 사라졌지만 역사는 보존되었다는 흐름을 설명하는 글이에요.

items.title: Forecasts and Doubt
items.text: Many people joke that weather forecasts are always wrong, but the truth is more interesting. A forecast of rain tomorrow is right most of the time, because computers can track large systems of clouds and wind across the whole planet. The further into the future we look, however, the less reliable the prediction becomes. Small errors in today's measurements grow bigger each day, so a seven-day forecast is much less certain than a one-day forecast. This is why forecasters often say 'a 30 percent chance of rain' instead of 'it will rain'. The number does not mean that it will rain on thirty percent of the city; it means that, on days with similar conditions, rain fell about three times out of ten. People who ignore this advice may feel cheated when a sunny day follows a warning. In fact, the forecast may have been correct. A fair judgment requires many days, not one.

qs.q: Why is a seven-day forecast less certain than a one-day forecast?
o: Computers cannot track clouds for more than a single day.
Small measurement errors grow larger as time passes.
Forecasters stop working after the first day of the week.
Wind systems disappear after twenty-four hours have passed.
qs.why: 'Small errors in today's measurements grow bigger each day'라고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about a '30 percent chance of rain' when the day stays dry?
o: The forecast may still have been a fair one.
The forecaster made a serious mistake.
The computers failed to work that day.
The rain fell in another part of the planet.
qs.why: 30% 확률은 비가 안 올 수도 있다는 뜻이므로 맑아도 예보가 틀렸다고 단정할 수 없어요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'reliable' means...
o: able to be trusted.
easy to understand.
pleasant to hear.
quick to change.
qs.why: reliable은 '믿을 수 있는'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'it means that, on days with similar conditions, rain fell about three times out of ten', what does 'it' refer to?
o: the city where the rain fell
the sunny day that followed
the warning given to the public
the number in a forecast
qs.why: 앞 문장의 'The number'(예보의 숫자)를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Weather cannot be predicted at all beyond the present day.
Computers will soon make human forecasters unnecessary.
People should plan their days without checking any forecasts.
Forecasts are more reliable than many people think.
qs.why: 예보가 대체로 맞고 확률 표현을 바르게 이해해야 한다는 것이 요지예요.

items.title: A Word Is Added
items.text: Every year, dictionary editors announce a list of new words, and every year some readers protest. They believe a dictionary should protect the language, not follow its changes. The editors disagree. A dictionary, they say, is like a map: it does not decide where the roads go, it records where people actually walk. A word is added only after careful observation. Editors collect examples from books, news articles and speech, and they wait to see whether the word appears for several years in many different places. A funny expression used by a few friends for one summer will not qualify. For example, 'selfie' entered dictionaries only after it had become common in several countries. Some words also leave the book when nobody uses them, although this happens slowly. Critics may still complain, but the process is a record of the community's habits rather than a judgment about good or bad English.

qs.q: When do dictionary editors add a word?
o: As soon as a famous speaker says it once.
Whenever a group of friends invents it.
After it has been used widely over several years.
Only when readers vote for it each summer.
qs.why: 여러 해 동안 여러 곳에서 쓰인 것을 확인한 뒤에 추가한다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the writer's attitude toward the readers who protest?
o: The writer agrees that new words spoil the language.
The writer thinks they misunderstand the purpose of a dictionary.
The writer believes they should edit the dictionary themselves.
The writer is angry that they read dictionaries.
qs.why: 사전이 언어를 심판하지 않고 기록한다고 설명하는 것은 항의하는 독자가 사전의 목적을 오해한다는 입장이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'qualify' means...
o: to meet the conditions for being accepted.
to be spoken in a quiet voice.
to be translated into another language.
to become longer after a while.
qs.why: qualify는 자격(조건)을 충족하다는 뜻이에요. 몇몇 친구만 한 여름 동안 쓴 표현은 조건에 못 미쳐요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'it does not decide where the roads go', what does 'it' refer to?
o: the language
the dictionary editor
a map
the community
qs.why: 비유에서 'A dictionary is like a map: it does not decide...'의 it은 지도를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does the writer compare a dictionary to a map?
o: To explain how to find words in alphabetical order.
To show that it records what people do rather than controlling it.
To suggest that dictionaries are hard to carry.
To prove that old words are more useful than new ones.
qs.why: 지도는 길을 정하지 않고 사람들이 걷는 곳을 기록한다는 비유로, 사전이 기록자라는 점을 보여 줘요.

items.title: Electric Buses
items.text: When the city bought its first fifty electric buses, many riders noticed the difference right away. The ride was quieter, and the air near the bus stops smelled cleaner. Drivers said that the buses were also smoother to control. Behind the scenes, though, the change was not simple. The new buses needed charging stations, and building them took almost two years. A fully charged bus could travel only about two hundred kilometers, so planners had to redesign some of the longest routes. Because the batteries are expensive, each bus cost almost twice as much as a diesel one. The city expects to save the difference over time, since electricity is cheaper than fuel and the motors need fewer repairs. Engineers also admit that making a battery uses a lot of energy. Even so, studies show that over its whole life, an electric bus produces far less pollution than a diesel bus. That is why the city plans to buy fifty more every year.

qs.q: Why did planners have to redesign some of the longest bus routes?
o: A charged bus can travel only about two hundred kilometers.
Riders had asked for a quieter ride on those routes.
Diesel fuel had become cheaper than electricity for the city.
The charging stations had been built too far apart.
qs.why: 한 번 충전으로 약 200km만 갈 수 있어서 긴 노선을 다시 설계해야 했다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the city's financial plan?
o: It expects riders to pay twice as much for their tickets.
It expects to sell the old diesel buses for a profit.
Lower running costs should make up for the higher price.
It expects the batteries to be free after two years.
qs.why: 전기가 연료보다 싸고 수리가 적어서 그 차액을 시간이 지나며 만회한다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'behind the scenes' means...
o: in the middle of a long theater show.
at the very front of the bus near the driver.
in the work that the public does not see.
during the busiest hour of the working day.
qs.why: behind the scenes는 '보이지 않는 곳에서, 막후에서'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'building them took almost two years', what does 'them' refer to?
o: the charging stations
the riders waiting at the stops
the older diesel buses
the longest bus routes in the city
qs.why: 'needed charging stations, and building them' — them은 충전소예요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the sentence 'Even so, studies show...'?
o: To prove that batteries use no energy at all.
To explain why the drivers enjoy their work so much.
To show that diesel buses are improving every year.
To balance an admitted weakness with an overall benefit.
qs.why: 배터리 제작에 에너지가 든다는 단점을 인정한 뒤, 전체적으로는 오염이 적다는 장점을 제시해요.

items.title: The Community Fridge
items.text: Outside a small café, there is a refrigerator that anyone can open. Neighbors leave extra vegetables, bread or cooked meals inside, and anyone who needs food can take what they like, with no questions asked. The idea began when a café owner noticed how much good food was thrown away at the end of each day. She wanted to give it a second chance, but a food bank was too far away. Within weeks, the fridge was emptied every evening. Some residents worry that the fridge might attract mice or spread illness, so volunteers wipe it clean daily and check the dates on every item. Others fear that people will take more than they need. In practice, this rarely happens; most users take one meal and leave a little something in return. The fridge has not solved hunger in the town, yet it has made neighbors talk to each other, and that, the owner says, is an unexpected gift.

qs.q: Why did the café owner start the community fridge?
o: A food bank nearby had asked her to open the fridge.
The town council had paid her to run a café.
Her neighbors were all unable to cook at home.
She saw that a lot of good food was being thrown away.
qs.why: 하루가 끝날 때 버려지는 음식이 많은 것을 보고 시작했다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the volunteers' daily cleaning?
o: It is required by the customers of the café.
It happens because the fridge is rarely used by anyone.
It is done so that mice can find some food.
It is meant to calm worries about health and safety.
qs.why: 쥐나 병이 생길 걱정에 대응하려고 매일 청소하고 날짜를 확인한다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'a second chance' means...
o: a faster delivery of bread to the shops.
another opportunity to be useful.
a higher price for good food in the market.
a longer walk from the café to the food bank.
qs.why: 버려질 음식에 다시 쓰일 기회를 준다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'In practice, this rarely happens', what does 'this' refer to?
o: the fridge being cleaned by volunteers every day
people taking more food than they need
mice getting into the café through the door
neighbors leaving extra vegetables inside the fridge
qs.why: 바로 앞의 우려 'people will take more than they need'를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What does the owner mean by calling the neighbors' conversations 'an unexpected gift'?
o: They are a benefit she did not plan when she began.
They show that the fridge is always completely full.
They are a present from the customers of the café.
They prove that hunger is solved in the whole town.
qs.why: 음식 나눔이 목적이었는데 이웃끼리 대화하게 된 것은 예상하지 못한 이점이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Washing Hands
items.text: In the middle of the nineteenth century, a doctor in a European hospital noticed something puzzling. Mothers who gave birth with the help of doctors were dying more often than those helped by midwives. He realized that the doctors often came straight from examining dead bodies. When he asked everyone to wash their hands with a special cleaning liquid, the number of deaths fell sharply. Surprisingly, many of his colleagues rejected his advice. They found the idea insulting, because no one had yet proved that invisible germs could cause disease. The doctor lost his position, and it was only years later, after scientists discovered bacteria, that his method was accepted. Today, hand washing is one of the simplest and cheapest ways to prevent illness. The story reminds us that a correct idea can be refused when it challenges what people already believe, and that evidence sometimes needs time to win.

qs.q: Why did the number of deaths fall in the doctor's hospital?
o: Midwives were no longer allowed to help with births.
Everyone began to wash their hands with a cleaning liquid.
The hospital moved into a cleaner new building.
Doctors stopped examining the mothers altogether.
qs.why: 의사들이 특수 세정액으로 손을 씻은 뒤 사망자가 크게 줄었다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the doctor's colleagues?
o: They were unable to read the scientific articles of that time.
They did not accept ideas that conflicted with their beliefs.
They had already discovered the bacteria themselves.
They preferred to work together with the midwives.
qs.why: 세균이 병을 일으킨다는 증거가 아직 없어서 이 생각을 모욕적으로 여기고 거부했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'puzzling' means...
o: clear and simple at first sight.
very frightening for the doctors.
hard to understand at first sight.
extremely funny to the patients.
qs.why: puzzling은 이해하기 어려운, 수수께끼 같은이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'They found the idea insulting', what does 'They' refer to?
o: the mothers in the hospital
the midwives who helped
the scientists who found bacteria
the doctor's colleagues
qs.why: 앞 문장 'many of his colleagues rejected his advice'를 받아요.

qs.q: What is the main point of the final sentence?
o: Doctors should never change their old habits in a hospital.
A true idea may be rejected for a long time before people accept it.
Hand washing is useful only in hospitals and nowhere else.
Evidence is always less important than what people believe.
qs.why: 옳은 생각도 기존 믿음과 부딪히면 거부될 수 있고 증거가 인정받기까지 시간이 걸린다는 결론이에요.

items.title: A Free Day
items.text: Once a month, the city art museum opens its doors without charging for tickets. The museum director explained the reason: many local families love art but find the price too high. On free days, the lines stretch around the corner, and the galleries are noisier than usual. Some regular visitors prefer the quiet of an ordinary weekday and avoid the crowds. Yet the director argues that crowds are exactly the point. Surveys show that a large share of free-day visitors had never entered the museum before. More than half of them later returned and paid for a ticket. This suggests that an open door can turn a stranger into a supporter. The museum does lose some ticket income on those days, but it gains donations and new members. For this reason, the director plans to add a free evening each week, as long as the building can handle the extra visitors safely.

qs.q: Why does the museum offer a free day each month?
o: The galleries are too quiet on ordinary weekdays.
Many local families find the ticket price too high.
The city has ordered the museum to close for a month.
Regular visitors have asked the museum for lower prices.
qs.why: 많은 지역 가족이 미술을 좋아하지만 가격이 비싸다고 느끼기 때문이라고 설명돼요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the visitors who 'returned and paid for a ticket'?
o: They disliked the crowds that gather on free days.
The free day gave them a reason to value the museum.
They received a free membership card at the door.
They had worked for the museum before the visit.
qs.why: 무료 입장이 낯선 사람을 후원자로 바꾼다는 결론이므로, 무료의 날이 박물관의 가치를 알게 했다고 볼 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'a supporter' is someone who...
o: draws pictures of the works inside a museum.
carries heavy objects for the visitors.
sells the tickets at the main entrance.
helps and stays loyal to an organization.
qs.why: supporter는 단체를 돕고 지지하는 사람을 뜻해요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'This suggests that an open door can turn a stranger into a supporter', what does 'This' refer to?
o: the noise that visitors make in the galleries
the director's plan for adding a free evening
the fact that over half of first-time visitors returned
the lines of visitors around the corner
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장의 설문 결과(절반 이상이 다시 와서 표를 샀다)를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the phrase 'as long as the building can handle the extra visitors safely'?
o: To explain why the museum is old.
To describe how visitors enter the galleries.
To criticize the survey results.
To set a condition for the director's plan.
qs.why: as long as는 조건을 뜻해서, 안전하게 수용할 수 있을 때만 계획한다는 조건이에요.

items.title: The Flat Cake
items.text: Mina had planned to bake a birthday cake for her grandmother, and she had followed the recipe carefully. But when she opened the oven, she found a flat, heavy disk. She was disappointed, and for a moment she wanted to buy a cake from the bakery. Instead, she checked the recipe again and noticed that she had forgotten the baking powder. That small ingredient, she realized, is what makes a cake rise. Because the shops were still open, she hurried out, bought a packet and started over. This time, she measured everything twice. The second cake was light and golden, though it was a little late. Her grandmother laughed when she heard the story and said that she would keep a slice of the flat cake too. 'A mistake that you understand,' she said, 'is worth more than a lucky success.' Mina agreed, and she wrote the lesson on the recipe card.

qs.q: Why did Mina's first cake come out flat?
o: She had forgotten the baking powder.
She opened the oven too early.
She measured the flour twice.
The oven was set at a low temperature.
qs.why: 레시피를 다시 확인하고 베이킹파우더를 빠뜨린 것을 알아챘다고 나와요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the grandmother's remark?
o: She dislikes cakes that rise too much in the oven.
She thinks Mina should buy cakes at a shop next time.
She values learning from errors more than avoiding them.
She believes that recipes are not very important.
qs.why: 이해한 실수가 운 좋은 성공보다 값지다는 말은 실수에서 배우는 것을 중시한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, 'disk' is used to describe the cake because it was...
o: round and thin.
tall and soft.
golden and sweet.
small and cold.
qs.why: flat, heavy disk는 둥글고 납작한 모양을 뜻해요.

qs.q: In the sentence 'That small ingredient, she realized, is what makes a cake rise', what does 'That small ingredient' refer to?
o: the recipe card
the sugar
the packet from the oven
the baking powder
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장에서 빠뜨렸다고 한 baking powder를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the story?
o: Understanding a mistake can be more valuable than getting lucky.
A cake from a bakery is always better than a homemade one.
Birthday cakes must be baked successfully in a single try.
Baking becomes easy when the oven is large enough.
qs.why: 마지막 할머니의 말과 Mina의 동의로 실수를 이해하는 것의 가치가 주제임을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: A Jacket Without a Receipt
items.text:
Customer: Hello. I'd like to return this jacket, but I can't find the receipt.
Clerk: I see. May I ask why you're returning it?
Customer: The sleeves are too long, so it doesn't fit me properly.
Clerk: That's a pity. Normally we need the receipt, since it proves that the jacket was bought here.
Customer: I understand, but the tag is still attached, and I paid by card.
Clerk: That helps, actually. If you give me the last four digits of your card, I can search for the purchase.
Customer: Of course. It's 4821.
Clerk: Here it is, from twelve days ago. Since it's within two weeks, I can offer you store credit.
Customer: Could I have a refund instead? I don't think I'll find anything else I like.
Clerk: Refunds need the receipt, but credit lasts a year, so you won't need to hurry.
Customer: In that case, store credit is fine. Thank you for your patience.

qs.q: Why does the clerk usually ask for a receipt?
o: It shows that the sleeves are too long.
It lets the shop search the customer's card.
It proves that the item was bought in that shop.
It tells the clerk how much store credit is left.
qs.why: 점원이 '영수증은 여기서 샀다는 증거'라고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about why the clerk could still help?
o: The customer had worn the jacket for more than two weeks.
The card payment gave another way to find the purchase.
The shop never checks the date of any purchase.
The tag proved that the jacket was a cheap one.
qs.why: 카드 끝 네 자리로 구매 기록을 찾을 수 있었기 때문에 영수증 없이도 도울 수 있었어요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'That's a pity' expresses...
o: sympathy for the customer's problem.
anger at the customer's request.
surprise at the price of the jacket.
approval of the customer's choice.
qs.why: That's a pity는 '안됐네요, 유감이네요'라는 동정을 나타내요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'it doesn't fit me properly'?
o: the jacket
the receipt
the tag
the card
qs.why: 문맥상 소매가 너무 길어 맞지 않는 것은 재킷이에요.

qs.q: What does the customer finally decide to do?
o: Look for the receipt at home first.
Exchange the jacket for a shorter one.
Accept store credit instead of money back.
Wait a year before choosing something else.
qs.why: 환불은 영수증이 필요해서 'store credit is fine'이라고 하며 상점 크레디트를 받아들여요.

items.title: Café or Tutoring
items.text:
Jihun: I got two job offers, and I can't decide. One is a café, and the other is tutoring middle school students.
Sora: What are the hours?
Jihun: The café needs me four evenings a week, but the tutoring is only two afternoons.
Sora: Then tutoring leaves more time for your own studying.
Jihun: True, but the café pays more per hour, and I'm saving for a laptop.
Sora: How much more?
Jihun: About three thousand won. That sounds small, but I'd work more hours at the café, and the café has tips.
Sora: Hmm, so the café could earn much more in total.
Jihun: Yes, although I'd come home late and be tired for class.
Sora: Then think about what matters more now. If grades are your priority, tutoring fits better.
Jihun: You're right. And tutoring would help me review my own math, so it has a double benefit.

qs.q: Why does Sora say tutoring leaves more time for studying?
o: It requires fewer working hours each week.
It pays less per hour than the café job does.
It takes place in the evenings only, after dinner.
It lets Jihun stop attending his own classes.
qs.why: 과외는 일주일에 오후 이틀뿐이라 공부할 시간이 더 남는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Jihun at the end?
o: He is leaning toward the tutoring job.
He has already accepted the job at the café.
He thinks that money does not matter at all.
He wants to refuse both of the job offers.
qs.why: Sora의 조언에 'You're right'라고 하고 과외의 이중 이점을 말하므로 과외 쪽으로 기울었어요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'a double benefit' means...
o: two good results from one choice.
a job that pays twice as much as another.
a discount on the price of two laptops.
two different jobs done at the same time.
qs.why: 과외로 돈도 벌고 자기 수학 복습도 되므로 한 선택에서 두 가지 이득이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does 'That' refer to in 'That sounds small'?
o: the number of working days in a week
the price of the laptop that he wants
the length of a class at school
the difference in hourly pay
qs.why: 바로 앞의 'About three thousand won', 즉 시급 차이를 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is Sora's main purpose in the last turns of the conversation?
o: To persuade Jihun to buy a new laptop at once.
To help Jihun decide by thinking about his priorities.
To complain about the long hours of both jobs.
To ask Jihun to find her a part-time job too.
qs.why: Sora는 무엇이 더 중요한지 생각해 보라며 우선순위에 따라 결정하도록 도와요.

items.title: Poster Promises
items.text:
Dana: I've finished my election poster, but I'm not sure about the slogan. It says 'Better lunches for everyone'.
Eli: It sounds nice, but isn't it too general? Students may ask how you'll do it.
Dana: Good point. I could add that I'll ask the cafeteria for a monthly vote on the menu.
Eli: That's much clearer. A promise with a method is more believable.
Dana: Should I also promise a longer lunch break?
Eli: I wouldn't. The council can't change the schedule, so you might not keep that promise.
Dana: Then it would hurt my credibility later.
Eli: Exactly. Smaller promises that you can keep are better than big ones that sound exciting.
Dana: All right. I'll write 'monthly menu vote' in large letters.
Eli: And maybe add a photo of last year's lunch survey as an example. Numbers make people trust you.
Dana: Great idea. Thanks for being honest with me.

qs.q: Why does Eli say the original slogan is 'too general'?
o: It does not mention the school lunch at all.
It is far too long to fit on a poster.
It promises something that the council cannot change.
It does not explain how the promise will be kept.
qs.why: 학생들이 '어떻게 할 건데?'라고 물을 수 있다고 하며 방법이 빠져 있음을 지적해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the 'longer lunch break' promise?
o: Eli believes that most students dislike school lunch.
Eli wants Dana to make even more promises.
Eli thinks it is outside the council's power.
Dana has already put that promise on her poster.
qs.why: 의회가 일정을 바꿀 수 없다고 했으므로 위원회 권한 밖이라고 보는 거예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'credibility' means...
o: the amount of money in a fund.
the ability to draw well.
the size of a school council.
the quality of being trusted.
qs.why: credibility는 신뢰성, 믿을 만한 정도를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does 'that' refer to in 'That's much clearer'?
o: the original slogan on the poster
last year's survey about lunch
the idea of a longer lunch break
Dana's idea of a monthly menu vote
qs.why: Dana가 방금 제안한 '매달 메뉴 투표'를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does Eli suggest adding a photo of last year's survey?
o: To make the poster look more colorful and attractive.
To give evidence that makes the poster more convincing.
To show that Dana took the survey by herself.
To compare this year's lunches with last year's.
qs.why: 'Numbers make people trust you' - 근거를 보여 설득력을 높이려는 것이에요.

items.title: Two Calendars
items.text:
Haru: The science fair is on the fifteenth, and my soccer team has a match on the same day.
Gina: That's unlucky. Which one matters more to you?
Haru: I'd love to do both, but the fair starts at nine and the match at one.
Gina: Then it's possible! The fair judges the projects in the morning, right?
Haru: Yes, but the awards ceremony is at noon, and the match field is across town.
Gina: So you could present, then leave before the ceremony.
Haru: If I leave early, I might miss a prize, though.
Gina: Perhaps you could ask the organizer if the judging can be earlier.
Haru: Hmm, that wouldn't be fair to the other students.
Gina: Then talk to your coach. Maybe you can arrive an hour late for the warm-up.
Haru: That seems reasonable. I'll message him tonight.

qs.q: Why does Haru hesitate about leaving the science fair early?
o: The match field is too close to the school.
His project has not been finished.
He dislikes the judges at the fair.
He might miss the awards ceremony.
qs.why: 일찍 떠나면 상을 놓칠 수 있다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Haru's reaction to asking for earlier judging?
o: He believes that the judges will refuse his request.
He wants to skip the soccer match altogether.
He thinks it would treat other students unfairly.
He has already asked the organizer for earlier judging.
qs.why: 'that wouldn't be fair to the other students'라고 해서 불공평하다고 생각해요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'warm-up' refers to...
o: light exercise done before a match.
a short speech that is given before a prize.
a meal that is eaten after a long game.
a meeting that is held after school.
qs.why: warm-up은 경기 전에 하는 준비 운동이에요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'Then it's possible!'?
o: doing both the fair and the match
winning a prize at the science fair
the awards ceremony that begins at noon
the soccer field across the town
qs.why: Gina는 시간이 다르므로 과학 박람회와 경기를 둘 다 하는 것이 가능하다고 말해요.

qs.q: What is Gina's purpose in suggesting that Haru talk to his coach?
o: To tell Haru to quit the soccer team for now.
To ask the coach to move the match to another day.
To offer a solution that does not harm anyone else.
To avoid giving Haru any advice about his plan.
qs.why: 공정성 문제가 없는 방법으로 코치에게 늦게 도착해도 되는지 묻자고 제안해요.

items.title: The Quiet Floor
items.text:
Ayla: Excuse me, are you the librarian? There's a group talking loudly on the third floor.
Librarian: Thank you for telling me. That floor is marked as a quiet zone.
Ayla: I know, but they've been there for an hour.
Librarian: Have you asked them to lower their voices?
Ayla: Not yet. I thought they might be annoyed.
Librarian: People often don't realize how far their voices travel, so a polite request usually works.
Ayla: What if they refuse?
Librarian: Then come back and I'll speak to them. But I'd try first. Complaining to staff can feel less friendly.
Ayla: You're right. Besides, if they know me, they might be quieter next time.
Librarian: Exactly. And if you need silence urgently, the study rooms on the second floor are free this afternoon.
Ayla: Thanks. I'll go and talk to them first.

qs.q: Why does the librarian suggest asking the group politely first?
o: The group is already planning to leave the library soon.
People often do not realize how far their voices travel.
The library has no rule about noise on any floor.
Staff are not allowed to speak to the visitors.
qs.why: 목소리가 멀리 퍼지는 줄 모르는 경우가 많아서 정중한 부탁이 보통 통한다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Ayla at the start?
o: She enjoys listening to the loud talk of others.
She works as a helper at the library herself.
She plans to leave the library at once.
She hesitated to speak to the group herself.
qs.why: 'I thought they might be annoyed'로 보아 직접 말하기를 망설였어요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'urgently' means...
o: in a very quiet and polite manner.
after a long delay of several hours.
as something that cannot wait.
without any help from other people.
qs.why: urgently는 '급하게, 미룰 수 없이'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does 'they' refer to in 'they might be quieter next time'?
o: the staff who work at the library
the study rooms on the second floor
Ayla and the librarian together
the people in the loud group
qs.why: 'if they know me'의 they와 같은 대상, 즉 떠드는 모임의 사람들이에요.

qs.q: What is Ayla's main reason for talking to the librarian?
o: To report a noise problem in a quiet zone.
To ask where the study rooms are located.
To return a book that is long overdue.
To learn how to speak more quietly.
qs.why: 3층 조용한 구역에서 큰 소리로 떠드는 문제를 알리려는 것이에요.

items.title: Tired Eyes
items.text:
Nurse: Your note says your eyes hurt in the afternoon. How many hours do you spend on a screen?
Student: Maybe seven or eight, because I study online and then play games.
Nurse: That's a lot. When you stare at a screen, you blink less often, so your eyes become dry.
Student: Is that why they feel itchy?
Nurse: Likely, yes. Dry eyes also get tired more quickly.
Student: What can I do? I can't stop studying.
Nurse: You don't need to. Try the twenty-twenty-twenty rule: every twenty minutes, look at something twenty feet away for twenty seconds.
Student: That sounds easy. Will it really help?
Nurse: It gives the eye muscles a rest, so the effect is usually noticeable within a week.
Student: What if the pain continues?
Nurse: Then see an eye doctor, since glasses might be needed.
Student: I'll try the rule first. Thank you.

qs.q: According to the nurse, why do the student's eyes feel dry?
o: Staring at a screen makes people blink less often.
Playing games makes the eyes water too much.
Studying online lowers the temperature of the room.
The student has not been wearing glasses at school.
qs.why: 화면을 볼 때 눈을 덜 깜빡여 건조해진다고 설명해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the nurse's advice on the 20-20-20 rule?
o: It is a simple habit that does not require giving up study.
It is a medicine that must be taken every week.
It replaces the need for ever seeing an eye doctor.
It works only for people who never play games.
qs.why: 공부를 그만두지 않아도 되는 간단한 습관으로 소개돼요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'noticeable' means...
o: difficult to describe.
easy to see or feel.
free of cost.
suitable for children.
qs.why: noticeable은 알아차릴 수 있을 만큼 뚜렷한 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'Will it really help?'
o: the eye doctor mentioned later
the itchy feeling in the eyes
the twenty-twenty-twenty rule
the games the student plays
qs.why: 학생은 방금 소개받은 20-20-20 규칙이 효과가 있는지 묻는 거예요.

qs.q: Why does the nurse mention glasses at the end?
o: To tell the student to stop wearing glasses.
To warn that screens can damage a pair of glasses.
To suggest that games always cause bad eyesight.
To explain a possible reason for continuing pain.
qs.why: 통증이 계속되면 안경이 필요할 수도 있기 때문에 안과에 가라고 하는 거예요.

items.title: Waiting for the 5:40
items.text:
Rui: The board says the 5:40 train to the coast is delayed by thirty minutes.
Kai: Then we'll miss the ferry at seven. Should we take the bus instead?
Rui: The bus takes ninety minutes, so we'd arrive at the same time as the late train.
Kai: Yes, but the train might be delayed even longer. Nobody knows.
Rui: True, though the bus can also get stuck in traffic on Friday evenings.
Kai: Hmm. Let's check the app. It says the train's problem is a signal fault, which can be fixed quickly.
Rui: Then waiting seems reasonable. If they announce another delay, we can switch to the bus.
Kai: But the bus station is a twenty-minute walk away, so we'd lose time.
Rui: Fine. We'll buy a snack and wait, and if the delay grows beyond an hour, we'll book a different ferry.
Kai: That's a sensible plan. Let's keep the tickets flexible.
Rui: I'll check the ferry company's change policy right now.

qs.q: Why is taking the bus not clearly better than waiting?
o: It would arrive about when the late train does.
It would cost much more than the train ticket.
It leaves from a station right next to the platform.
It runs only on Friday evenings, not at other times.
qs.why: 버스는 90분이 걸려 지연된 기차와 비슷한 시각에 도착한다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the signal fault?
o: It will probably last until late at night.
It was caused by heavy traffic on Friday evening.
It affects only the bus service to the coast.
It is expected to be fixed quickly.
qs.why: 앱에서 '빨리 고칠 수 있다'고 해서 기다리기로 합리적으로 판단하게 돼요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'flexible' tickets are ones that...
o: cost nothing to buy at the station.
can be changed if plans change.
are valid on every train in the country.
must be used right away on the same day.
qs.why: flexible은 계획이 바뀌면 변경할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'It says the train's problem is a signal fault'?
o: the app
the board
the bus
the ferry
qs.why: 'Let's check the app. It says...'에서 it은 앱이에요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the speakers' conversation?
o: To complain about the ferry company's rules.
To decide how to handle a delay without losing their trip.
To buy snacks while the train is arriving.
To plan the exact route of the long bus ride.
qs.why: 기차 지연에 대비해 여행을 망치지 않을 방법을 정하는 대화예요.

items.title: Can I Trust These Reviews
items.text:
Nari: I want to buy these headphones. They have 4.8 stars, so they must be great.
Omar: How many reviews are there?
Nari: Only twelve, but they're all very positive.
Omar: That might be a warning sign. A small number of reviews can be unreliable.
Nari: Why? Every reviewer gave five stars.
Omar: Exactly. Real opinions usually vary, so perfect scores can mean that the seller wrote some of them.
Nari: I hadn't thought of that. How can I tell?
Omar: Look for detailed reviews with pros and cons, and check whether the dates are all the same.
Nari: Several were posted on the same day. And they all use the word 'amazing'.
Omar: That does look suspicious. Compare them with the reviews of a model that has hundreds, even if its score is only 4.4.
Nari: A lower score from more people might be more honest, then.
Omar: Right. You'd get a truer picture.

qs.q: Why does Omar think perfect scores can be a warning sign?
o: Real opinions usually vary from person to person.
Headphones rarely receive any reviews from buyers.
Sellers are not allowed to read the reviews of their goods.
Customers prefer to buy products without any stars.
qs.why: 진짜 의견은 보통 다양하기 때문에 전부 만점이면 판매자가 쓴 것일 수 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the twelve reviews?
o: Some may have been written by the seller.
All of them describe both good and bad points.
They were posted over several months.
They compare many different models.
qs.why: 같은 날 올라오고 같은 단어를 반복해서 수상하다고 했으므로 판매자가 썼을 가능성이 있어요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'suspicious' means...
o: proving without any doubt that something is true.
causing laughter among all the readers.
making people doubt that something is honest.
causing hunger after a long day.
qs.why: suspicious는 정직성에 의심이 가는, 수상한이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does 'them' refer to in 'Compare them with the reviews of a model'?
o: the hundreds of reviews of another model
the stars shown beside the price
the dates shown at the top of the page
the twelve reviews of the headphones
qs.why: Omar는 Nari가 본 12개의 후기를 후기가 많은 다른 모델과 비교하라고 해요.

qs.q: What is the main point Omar wants to make?
o: Cheaper headphones are always the best choice for anyone.
A perfect score means little without many varied reviews.
Reviews should never be read before you buy a product.
A product with only 4.4 stars should always be avoided.
qs.why: 점수만 보지 말고 후기의 수와 다양성으로 신뢰성을 판단해야 한다는 것이 핵심이에요.

items.title: Compost or Trash
items.text:
Lena: Mr. Ortiz, I noticed you put the vegetable scraps in a bin in the corner. Is that compost?
Mr. Ortiz: Yes. In a few months, those scraps become rich soil for the garden.
Lena: Doesn't it smell?
Mr. Ortiz: It would if I added meat or fish, but I only use plant waste, so it smells earthy, like a forest.
Lena: And what do you do with the soil?
Mr. Ortiz: I mix it into the flower beds. The plants grow stronger, so I buy less fertilizer.
Lena: That's a clever way to save money. Is it difficult?
Mr. Ortiz: Not at all. You turn the pile once a week so air can get in. Without air, it rots slowly and does smell bad.
Lena: Hmm. I live in an apartment, though. I only have a balcony.
Mr. Ortiz: You can still try. A small closed container works if you keep it dry.
Lena: Then I might start with a small box.

qs.q: According to Mr. Ortiz, why does his compost not smell bad?
o: He keeps the bin far away from the flower beds.
He mixes it with fertilizer once each month.
He covers it tightly so that no air can enter.
He adds only plant waste and turns the pile for air.
qs.why: 식물성 쓰레기만 넣고 공기가 들어가게 뒤집어 주기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Lena at the end?
o: She is interested in composting despite her small space.
She has already filled a large compost pile at home.
She plans to move to a house with a big garden.
She thinks composting is far too expensive.
qs.why: 아파트라 베란다뿐이지만 작은 상자로 시작해 볼까 한다고 해요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'earthy' describes a smell that is...
o: like soil.
like soap.
like smoke.
like sugar.
qs.why: earthy는 흙 같은 냄새를 말하며, 숲 같다는 설명이 힌트예요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'Without air, it rots slowly'?
o: the compost pile
the balcony of her apartment
the fertilizer bought in a shop
the flower bed in the garden
qs.why: 공기가 없으면 퇴비 더미가 천천히 썩는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is Mr. Ortiz's purpose in the last part of the conversation?
o: To sell Lena a container for use on her balcony.
To show Lena that her small space is not a barrier.
To warn Lena that apartments forbid all compost.
To end the conversation as politely as possible.
qs.why: 베란다만 있어도 작은 밀폐 용기로 가능하다고 말해 Lena를 격려해요.

items.title: Saturday at the Shelter
items.text:
Coordinator: Thanks for coming, Pablo. Can you help at the animal shelter on Saturdays?
Pablo: I'd like to, but I have a swimming lesson in the morning.
Coordinator: We need people most in the morning, because that's when the dogs are fed and walked.
Pablo: Then Sunday might be better. Do you have any tasks then?
Coordinator: Sundays are for cleaning cages. It's less fun than walking dogs, though just as important.
Pablo: I don't mind. A clean cage is good for the animals, so I'd feel useful.
Coordinator: Wonderful. If you come every week, the dogs will recognize you, which helps shy ones feel safe.
Pablo: Really? That's a good reason to be regular.
Coordinator: Yes. But if you can't come one week, just tell us, so we can arrange a replacement.
Pablo: Of course. I'll send a message the day before.
Coordinator: Perfect. Let's start next Sunday at nine.

qs.q: Why does the coordinator prefer volunteers on Saturday mornings?
o: The dogs are fed and walked at that time.
The shelter closes completely on Sunday.
Cages are cleaned only in the morning hours.
Swimming lessons for volunteers begin on Saturdays.
qs.why: 토요일 오전에 개들에게 먹이를 주고 산책시키기 때문에 일손이 가장 필요해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Pablo's attitude toward cleaning cages?
o: He dislikes animals but he needs a job.
He is willing to do it because it helps the animals.
He will also walk dogs in addition to cleaning.
He wants to clean only the largest cages.
qs.why: 'I don't mind. A clean cage is good for the animals'라고 하며 기꺼이 하겠다고 해요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'regular' means...
o: coming at the same times each week.
bigger than the average size of volunteers.
strong enough to carry heavy cages.
completely free of charge for everyone.
qs.why: regular는 규칙적으로 정해진 때에 오는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does 'which' refer to in 'which helps shy ones feel safe'?
o: the cleaning of the cages every Sunday morning
the feeding of the dogs in the morning
the dogs recognizing a volunteer who comes every week
the message that Pablo sends the day before
qs.why: which는 앞 절 전체, 즉 매주 오는 사람을 개들이 알아보는 일을 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does the coordinator ask Pablo to send a message when he cannot come?
o: So that Pablo can choose a different animal to care for.
So that the dogs will learn to recognize his voice.
So that the shelter can find someone to take his place.
So that the shelter can close for the whole day.
qs.why: 대체 인력을 구하기 위해 미리 알려 달라는 것이에요.

items.title: Cards or Quizzes
items.text:
Minho: I've been using flashcards for vocabulary, but I keep forgetting the words by the weekend.
Tara: Do you test yourself, or just read them?
Minho: I mostly read them. It feels like studying.
Tara: It feels that way, but reading is passive. Research suggests that trying to recall a word works better.
Minho: So practice quizzes are more effective?
Tara: Yes, because struggling to remember makes the memory stronger.
Minho: That's surprising. Quizzes feel harder, so I assumed they were worse.
Tara: The difficulty is exactly the point. Easy review gives a false sense of progress.
Minho: Still, flashcards are portable, and I can use them on the bus.
Tara: Then use them for testing. Cover one side and guess before turning the card.
Minho: That way I get the convenience and the benefit.
Tara: Exactly. Try it for a week and compare the results.

qs.q: According to Tara, why are practice quizzes more effective than reading?
o: Quizzes are easier and more enjoyable than reading.
Struggling to recall a word strengthens the memory.
Quizzes let students use the time spent on the bus.
Reading flashcards is not allowed in some classes.
qs.why: 기억해 내려고 애쓰는 과정이 기억을 더 단단하게 만든다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Minho's earlier belief?
o: He thought that quizzes were boring to write.
He believed that reading cards is impossible.
He had never before tried to use flashcards.
He assumed an easier method must be better.
qs.why: 퀴즈가 더 어려워서 오히려 나쁘다고 생각했다고 했으므로 쉬운 방법이 더 좋다고 가정했어요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'passive' means...
o: done in public places like a bus.
not involving active effort.
done very fast without any pauses.
done together with other people.
qs.why: passive는 능동적인 노력이 들지 않는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'It feels like studying'?
o: reading the flashcards
taking a practice quiz
riding the bus
remembering the weekend
qs.why: 민호는 카드를 읽기만 한다고 했고, 그것이 공부처럼 느껴진다는 거예요.

qs.q: What is Tara's main advice at the end?
o: Keep using flashcards, but use them to test yourself.
Stop using flashcards completely and buy a book.
Study only on the weekend with a friend.
Read each card twice before you turn it over.
qs.why: 카드의 한쪽을 가리고 맞혀 보는 식으로, 카드를 쓰되 스스로 테스트하라는 조언이에요.

items.title: Secondhand Bike
items.text:
Yuri: I found a used bike online for eighty thousand won. A new one costs three times as much.
Dev: That's a big difference. What condition is it in?
Yuri: The photos look fine, but the seller says the brakes are a little old.
Dev: Brakes matter for safety, so I'd be careful. Replacing them might cost twenty thousand.
Yuri: Even so, it would still be cheaper than a new bike.
Dev: True, but there might be other problems, like rust inside the chain.
Yuri: That's possible. Could you come with me to look at it?
Dev: Sure. I'd check the tires, the chain and the brakes, and ask why the owner is selling it.
Yuri: Why ask that?
Dev: If the owner sells it because it keeps breaking, you'd want to know.
Yuri: Good thinking. I'll arrange a time this weekend.

qs.q: Why does Dev advise being careful about the brakes?
o: Brakes are important for the rider's safety.
They are the most expensive part of any bike.
They are always old on every used bike.
They cannot be replaced after the purchase.
qs.why: 브레이크는 안전에 중요하기 때문에 조심해야 한다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the used bike's total price if the brakes are replaced?
o: It would be the same as a new bike.
It would be free of charge.
It would be about one hundred thousand won.
It would be about three hundred thousand won.
qs.why: 80,000원에 수리비 약 20,000원을 더하면 약 100,000원이에요. 새 자전거는 약 240,000원이에요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'condition' means...
o: the price of an object.
the state of an object.
the color of an object.
the owner of an object.
qs.why: What condition is it in?은 물건의 상태를 묻는 질문이에요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'ask why the owner is selling it'?
o: the chain of the bike
the used bike
the new bike in the shop
the weekend visit
qs.why: 주인이 파는 물건은 중고 자전거예요.

qs.q: Why does Dev suggest asking the owner why the bike is for sale?
o: To learn the owner's full name and address.
To get a lower price on the new bike.
To make the owner feel guilty about selling.
To find out whether the bike has hidden problems.
qs.why: 계속 고장나서 파는 것인지 알면 숨은 문제를 알 수 있기 때문이에요.

items.title: Extra Time
items.text:
Student: Ms. Wells, may I speak with you about the history essay?
Ms. Wells: Of course. What's the problem?
Student: I need two more days. I had a fever last week and lost three days of work.
Ms. Wells: I'm sorry you were sick. Do you have a note from a doctor?
Student: Yes, I brought one. I wanted to ask before the deadline, not after.
Ms. Wells: I appreciate that. Asking in advance shows responsibility.
Student: Thank you. I know the deadline is fair for everyone else.
Ms. Wells: It is, but illness is a good reason. I can give you until Thursday.
Student: That would be great. Should I send the essay by email?
Ms. Wells: Yes, and write the date in the subject line so I don't lose it.
Student: I'll do that. I won't ask again unless there's an emergency.
Ms. Wells: I trust you. Now, how is the essay going?

qs.q: Why does Ms. Wells agree to give extra time?
o: The essay topic was far too difficult for everyone.
The student was ill and asked before the deadline.
The student had finished most of the writing already.
Other students had also asked for more days.
qs.why: 아파서 사흘을 잃었고 마감 전에 미리 요청했기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Ms. Wells' attitude?
o: She never changes deadlines for any student.
She is flexible when a student has a genuine reason.
She does not read the essays of her students.
She dislikes receiving emails from her students.
qs.why: 병이라는 타당한 이유가 있으면 기한을 연장해 주므로 합당한 이유엔 융통성이 있어요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'in advance' means...
o: before something happens.
after something happens.
instead of something else.
at the same time.
qs.why: in advance는 '미리'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'It is, but illness is a good reason'?
o: the deadline
the essay
the doctor's note
the email
qs.why: 앞 학생의 말 'the deadline is fair'에서 이어지는 it이에요.

qs.q: Why does the student bring a doctor's note?
o: To prove that the essay is already finished.
To ask for a different topic for the essay.
To support the request with evidence.
To thank the teacher for her kind help.
qs.why: 병이 있었다는 증거를 보여 요청을 뒷받침하기 위해서예요.

items.title: Hamster or Fish
items.text:
Sena: Mom said we can get one pet, and I want a hamster.
Tomás: I'd prefer fish. They are quiet, and they don't need walks or cuddles.
Sena: But a hamster is more fun to play with.
Tomás: It's also more work. A hamster needs fresh food and water every day, and its cage needs cleaning.
Sena: Fish need cleaning too. The tank gets green.
Tomás: Less often, though. And a hamster sleeps in the day, so you'd see it only at night.
Sena: Hmm, I hadn't considered that. I'd be at school then, and asleep.
Tomás: Exactly. You'd see it for maybe an hour a day. A fish is active when we're awake.
Sena: That's a fair point. But I still like holding a small animal.
Tomás: How about a compromise? We start with fish, and if we take care of them well, Mom might agree to a hamster later.
Sena: That sounds sensible. A good record would convince her.

qs.q: Why does Tomás think a hamster is more work than fish?
o: It needs fresh food and water daily and cage cleaning.
It must be walked outside every afternoon.
It needs a tank that turns green each week.
It cannot be kept together with other pets.
qs.why: 햄스터는 매일 신선한 먹이와 물이 필요하고 우리도 청소해야 한다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Sena's change of mind during the conversation?
o: She no longer likes any kind of pet at all.
She has decided to buy a hamster tomorrow.
She now accepts that waiting for a hamster may be wise.
She now thinks that fish are more fun to hold.
qs.why: 합리적인 지적을 받아들이고 먼저 물고기를 키운 뒤 햄스터를 고려하는 절충안에 동의해요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, 'a compromise' is...
o: a choice made quickly without thinking about it.
a rule that is imposed by a parent.
a gift that is given by a friend.
a middle choice that satisfies both sides somewhat.
qs.why: 물고기 먼저, 나중에 햄스터라는 절충안을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does 'it' refer to in 'It's also more work'?
o: keeping a hamster
keeping fish
getting permission
joining a pet club
qs.why: Sena가 햄스터가 재미있다고 한 말에 대한 반박으로, 햄스터를 키우는 일을 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does Tomás say a hamster is seen 'only at night'?
o: To prove that all hamsters are dangerous animals.
To explain why fish are cheaper than hamsters.
To argue that a hamster is awake at the wrong times for them.
To show that Sena sleeps during the daytime.
qs.why: 햄스터는 낮에 자기 때문에 학교와 수면 시간과 겹쳐 함께할 시간이 적다는 주장을 뒷받침해요.
